te: Meeting summary video · Thai–Sri Lankan labour cooperation, and a proposal on employing persons with disabilities
Report on migrant workers, the case of Ranong, prepared for the Senate
se: The meeting agreed to refer a petition requesting support for the Huai Pha Daeng reservoir project in Chiang Mai Province to the committee concerned, as it is not directly within its duties and powers, and prepared to present its study report on managing migrant workers, a case study of Ranong Province (7 proposals to the government), to the Senate on 28 September 2026. It also followed up the subcommittees' work
it: Petition: request for support for the Huai Pha Daeng reservoir project, Doi Tao Subdistrict, Chiang Mai Province
Presentation of the study report on managing migrant workers, a case study of Ranong Province, to the Senate on 28 September 2026
Subcommittees: 2 reports for the Senate (migrant workers in Ranong · a digital platform for labour development) · objections concerning international labour conventions

te: Start of collections for the Employee Welfare Fund, and an annual review seminar prepared
se: The meeting invited the Department of Labour Protection and Welfare to give information on a petition from employers' representatives asking for a review of the start of savings and contributions to the Employee Welfare Fund (from 1 October 2026, 0.25% of wages from each side), and agreed to forward the petition to the Ministry of Labour. It noted progress on the seminar reviewing work in fiscal year 2026 (11 September 2026) and the subcommittees' work
it: Petition: request to review the start of savings and contributions to the Employee Welfare Fund (the Department of Labour Protection and Welfare invited to give information)
Seminar "Review of Work in Fiscal Year 2026 and Draft Plan for Fiscal Year 2027", 11 September 2026
Subcommittees: plan for fiscal year 2027 · proposals on 3 draft labour protection Acts · the issue of moving medical benefits to the Universal Coverage Scheme

te: Objections concerning the signing of international labour conventions, and a seminar reviewing fiscal year 2026 prepared
se: The meeting considered a letter objecting to the proposal to sign international labour conventions and a request for measures limiting the validity of status documents for children of migrant workers born in Thailand, separating them into 3 issues and referring them to the subcommittees for further study. It considered the schedule of the seminar reviewing work in fiscal year 2026 and the plan for fiscal year 2027, and followed up the subcommittees' work
it: Letter objecting to the proposal to sign international labour conventions, and a request concerning status documents for children of migrant workers born in Thailand
Schedule of the seminar "Review of Work in Fiscal Year 2026 and Draft Plan for Fiscal Year 2027"
Following up the work of all 3 subcommittees (Employment Services and Skills Development · Labour Welfare and Protection · Social Security)

te: Special meeting: report on the sustainability of the Social Security Fund prepared for the Senate
se: At a special meeting on Monday 17 August 2026, the meeting considered the presentation of its study report on approaches to strengthening the sustainability of the Social Security Fund to the Senate (25 August 2026), noted the subcommittees' work, and approved Mr. Samart Rangsan, senator, as a committee member to fill a vacancy
it: Presentation of the study report on approaches to strengthening the sustainability of the Social Security Fund to the Senate on 25 August 2026
Following up the work of all 3 subcommittees (Employment Services and Skills Development · Labour Welfare and Protection · Social Security)
Mr. Samart Rangsan, senator, asks to join as a committee member

te: Bilateral meeting in Bangladesh, and the work of all three subcommittees
se: The meeting noted the subcommittees' work: an outline report reviewing the law on employing older persons, preparations for a seminar on independent and platform workers (18 August 2026), a seminar on restructuring the Social Security Office, and the issue of moving medical benefits to the Universal Coverage Scheme. It approved a trip for a bilateral meeting in the People's Republic of Bangladesh on 11–13 August 2026 at the invitation of the embassy, and appointed a committee secretary
it: Following up the work of all 3 subcommittees (Employment Services and Skills Development · Labour Welfare and Protection · Social Security)
Trip for a bilateral meeting and visit to the People's Republic of Bangladesh, 11–13 August 2026 (a delegation of 3, discussing Bangladeshi workers in the construction sector)
Appointment of a committee secretary to fill a vacancy
Proposal to appoint 8 honorary advisers noted

te: Seminar on restructuring the Social Security Office prepared, and work on older workers
se: The meeting followed up the subcommittees' work: approaches to labour and legal development for an ageing society (hearing about a post-retirement employment project from a professional association of human resources practitioners), preparations for a seminar on restructuring the Social Security Office (16 August 2026), a proposal that the Social Security Office become an independent body like the Government Pension Fund, the issue of moving insured persons' medical benefits to the Universal Coverage Scheme, and the schedule of discussions with Social Security Office executives on 6 August 2026
it: Subcommittee on Employment Services: approaches to labour and legal development for an ageing society

Subcommittee on Social Security: preparations for the seminar "Restructuring the Social Security Office", 16 August 2026 · proposal for an independent body · the issue of moving medical benefits to the Universal Coverage Scheme
Discussions with Social Security Office executives, 6 August 2026

te: Petition on the employment of migrant workers, and progress of the subcommittees on older persons, wages and pensions
se: The meeting considered a petition asking for an examination of the employment of migrant workers by a private company (as alleged), agreeing to request information from the Department of Employment and the Department of Labour Protection and Welfare. It followed up the subcommittees' work, such as an elderly fund, a study visit to Chiang Mai and Lamphun, wages in security service contracts, a seminar on platform workers, the pension formula under section 33, and reform of Social Security Fund management, and adjusted the list of advisers in line with the committee's regulations
it: Petition: request to examine the employment of migrant workers by a private company and the oversight of the agencies concerned
Subcommittee on Employment Services: elderly fund · study visit to Chiang Mai and Lamphun, 19–21 August 2026
Subcommittee on Labour Welfare: wages of security guards in government contracts · seminar on independent and platform workers
Subcommittee on Social Security: the section 33 old-age pension formula · working group on reforming the management of the Social Security Fund
Appointment of a committee secretary · lists of honorary advisers and subcommittee advisers adjusted in line with the committee's regulations

te: Report on the sustainability of the Social Security Fund prepared for the Senate, and a meeting with the Government Pension Fund set
se: The meeting considered preparations to present the working group's study report on approaches to strengthening the sustainability of the Social Security Fund to the Senate, approved the proposals of all 3 subcommittees, approved a meeting with executives of the Government Pension Fund (GPF) on 9 July 2026, and appointed a committee secretary to fill a vacancy
it: Preparations to present the study report on approaches to strengthening the sustainability of the Social Security Fund to the Senate
Progress of all 3 subcommittees
Meeting with executives of the Government Pension Fund, 9 July 2026
Appointment of a committee secretary to fill a vacancy

te: Report on independent and platform workers, and a proposal on wages in government service contracts
se: The meeting followed up the subcommittees' work: a draft study report on the problems of and solutions for independent and platform workers (with a seminar planned for about 200 people), and consideration of a petition on employment at minimum wage rates and government budget allocation, to be summarised as policy recommendations that protect employees' rights. It also considered approaches to preparing the committee's observations and reports
it: Draft study report: problems of and solutions for independent and platform workers
Petition: employment under the minimum wage notification and government budget allocation
Approaches to preparing observations and recommendations, and the committee's study reports

te: Minimum wage and government service contracts, and the section 39 pension formula in light of a Supreme Court judgment
se: The meeting considered a petition asking for solutions to problems of employment under the minimum wage notification and for fair government budget allocation, and a request for support to amend the law on the formula for calculating the old-age pension under section 39 so that it is calculated separately for each period, in line with Supreme Court Judgment No. 3307/2567. It noted progress on meetings with the ministers of both ministries and followed up the subcommittees' work
it: Petition: employment under the minimum wage notification and government budget allocation in service contracts
Request for support to amend the law on the formula for calculating the old-age pension under section 39 separately for each period, in line with Supreme Court Judgment No. 3307/2567
Schedule of meetings with the Minister of Labour and the Minister of Social Development and Human Security

Subcommittees: employing older persons · government service contracts (the Office of the Civil Service Commission, the Office of the Public Sector Development Commission, the Bureau of the Budget and the Comptroller General's Department invited to give information) · restructuring the Social Security Office

te: International labour standards, Thai–Japanese cooperation, and meetings with two ministers prepared
se: The meeting discussed raising labour standards to international level (International Labour Organization conventions) and the Thai–Japanese memorandum of cooperation (MOC) on a new system of employment for skills development approved by the Council of Ministers, prepared meetings with the Minister of Social Development and Human Security and the Minister of Labour (19 June 2026), and noted the subcommittee's study visit to Prachuap Khiri Khan Province
it: Raising labour standards to international level (International Labour Organization conventions and international cooperation)
Thai–Japanese memorandum of cooperation (MOC) on employment for skills development
Preparations for meetings with the Minister of Social Development and Human Security and the Minister of Labour
Study visit by the Subcommittee on Employment Services to Prachuap Khiri Khan Province (quality of life and careers of older persons)

te: The new old-age pension formula (CARE formula): advantages, disadvantages and effects on insured persons
se: The meeting invited agencies and those concerned to give information on the Social Security Office's new old-age pension formula (the CARE formula, which uses adjusted average career earnings instead of final wages), including its advantages, disadvantages, effects and ways to address them. It followed up the subcommittees' work and noted an idea for reforming the structure of the Social Security Office into a professionally managed organisation
it: The new old-age pension formula (CARE formula): advantages, disadvantages, effects on insured persons, and solutions
Petition: effects on businesses of government agencies' service contracts following wage adjustments
Plan to reform the structure of the Social Security Office to improve the quality of life of insured persons

te: Thai workers unable to return to work in Israel, and a study of Japanese-style employment of older persons
se: The meeting invited the Department of Employment to give information on a petition concerning Thai workers who were unable to report back for work in the State of Israel, and resolved to summarise the matter and inform the petitioner of the outcome. It followed up the subcommittees' work, such as studying approaches to employing older persons from Japan and hearing employers' and insured persons' representatives on restructuring the Social Security Office, and appointed honorary advisers
it: Petition: Thai workers unable to report back for work in the State of Israel (the Department of Employment invited to give information)
Subcommittees: approaches to employing older persons from Japan · appointment of 2 subcommittee member(s) to fill vacancies
Subcommittee on Social Security: employers' and insured persons' representatives heard on restructuring the Social Security Office
Appointment of honorary advisers to the committee
